sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as at the first giving of the Torah the world's stability was strengthened, so too each year the increase in receiving Torah adds to the world's stability, revealing the power of Atzmus that creates ex nihilo, which is the true meaning of "quiet," and this includes an increase in the three pillars, especially charity, which should be given on Shavuos eve as a new opening.

translations.translation: And behold,
just as at the giving of the Torah the first time there was a strengthening in the existence of the world, as the Sages said,
on the verse,
"The earth feared and was quiet,"
that until the sixth day of Sivan the earth feared,
and on the sixth day of Sivan,
when Israel received the Torah,
it was quiet,
so too is it in every single year,
that through the addition in the giving of Torah and the receiving of Torah, an addition is made in the strength of the world's existence.
And in the manner mentioned above
(section 3),
that through engaging in Torah in a manner that it is as new in your eyes, one also reveals the novelty that exists in the world,
which is renewed every moment from nothing to something by the power of the Awtsmoos.
For it can be said that this matter
[the revelation of the G-dly power that brings the world into being from nothing to something]
is the true essence of the concept of "quiet."
And based on this, one may add,
that this need to add each year in the preparations for the giving of Torah and the receiving of Torah,
includes within it also an addition in the three pillars upon which the world stands,
Torah, service, and acts of kindness.
And in particular in charity,
for in addition to it being one of the pillars of the world,
it is
(also)
the entirety of the entire Torah,
as explained in Torah Or, in the discourse beginning "In the third month."
Therefore, in addition to the conclusion
(as is customary)
of each and every one making themselves a messenger for the mitzvah of charity—it should be on the eve of the holiday of Shavuos,
the eve of the time of the giving of our Torah,
a special addition in the giving of charity,
to the extent that the giving of charity on this day should be in a manner of a new opening,
for through this opening there is also made an addition in the influence from His open hand
(the full, open, holy, and wide hand)
regarding all matters,
and in particular regarding the matter of the giving of the Torah,
beginning from the first utterance "I am G-d your Lord who took you out of the land of Egypt,"
that they go out from all constraints and boundaries,
and become one with the "I am" who gives the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This departure from constraints comes to the soul as it is clothed in the body, for long life and good years, and through studying both the revealed and inner dimensions of Torah, the body and soul become a single reality that is one with the "I am" who gives the Torah.

translations.translation: And this matter
(of going out from constraints and boundaries)
comes to the soul as it is clothed in the body,
for length of days and good years,
a healthy body and a healthy soul.
And through the study of the revealed aspect of Torah
(the body of Torah)
and the inner aspect of Torah
(the soul of Torah),
both of which are one Torah,
there is also made the body and soul of the person studying into a single existence,
an existence that is one with "I am,"
the Giver of the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: By proclaiming these matters in a great house, a house that magnifies Torah and prayer, there is an additional increase in all the above, that G-d helps fulfill all resolutions and requests for the preparations for the giving of Torah, leading to a completely new Torah that will go forth from Me in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach, for the giving of Torah is the giving of the Torah down on earth, not in heaven.

translations.translation: And by proclaiming these matters in a great house,
a house in which Torah is magnified,
and a house in which prayer is magnified,
for prayer is the request for all one's needs,
both one's spiritual needs and one's physical needs,
behold, through this there is added even more in all the above,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps to fulfill all the resolutions
(which are also a request and prayer)
of the preparations for the giving of the Torah,
and also fulfills the requests regarding the drawing down of the giving of the Torah
[and in particular that they are in a house in which Torah is magnified],
that the drawing down of the Torah will be in completeness and in an entirely new manner as above,
to the extent of "a new Torah from Me shall go forth"
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach.
And to add,
that the matter of the giving of the Torah is—the giving of the Torah down on earth,
and in a manner of "it is not in heaven."
And as the Sages said,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the ministering angels, "I and you will go to the earthly court, etc."
